A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–G support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original matrix-sensing and regression simulations, Olivetti faces sparse-coding experiments, ViT evaluations on ImageNet/CIFAR10, and GPT-2 LoRA results on tiny_shakespeare.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds regularization-schedule and switch-off-timing ablations in Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: The proposed mirror-flow framework, reparameterizations, regularized objectives and weight-decay switch-off strategy are retained. Additional schedules are evaluated as comparisons and ablations; no proposed algorithm or architecture is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions retain synthetic matrix sensing and regression, Olivetti faces sparse coding, ImageNet/CIFAR10 vision tasks and tiny_shakespeare fine-tuning. The new ablations vary scheduling within existing tasks.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix C adds linear and cosine weight-decay schedules to the matrix-sensing comparisons, beyond v1's constant and abrupt switch-off schedules. Existing comparison methods remain, including the learning-rate-scheduler comparisons already present in Appendix G.

E3.justification: The new matrix-sensing ablation extends matched-total-regularization comparisons to linear and cosine schedules, tests additional strengths, and reports time to a 1e-7 training-loss threshold. Appendix F varies switch-off points across 50, 100, 150 and 200 at weight decay 0.2. Existing protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Tables 2–3 test sensitivity to regularization schedule shape/strength and ViT switch-off timing. These are focused additions to existing experiments; the earlier deeper-parameterization, sparse-coding and learning-rate analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose three seeds for CIFAR10 and two for GPT-2, with unchanged ± reporting in the retained result tables. The new ablations add no run counts, uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds schedule-specific results, including reconstruction errors of 2.3e-4 and 2.1e-4 for linear and cosine decay in Table 2. Table 3 adds timing results, such as WD/Off validation accuracies of 70.7/72.4 for switch-off point 50. Existing plots and v1 Tables 2–3, now v2 Tables 4–5, retain their results.

T1.justification: v2 Theorem 3.6 explicitly imposes regularity and commutation on the joint map (g,h), replacing v1 Theorem 3.2's separate formulation. Appendix B revises the Hessian argument with explicit Schur-complement steps and corrects the Bregman-divergence gradient evaluation in B.2. Definitions reproduced in the main text already existed in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and discussion retain the same claims about three regularization effects, convergence and optimality, and improved generalization through switching off weight decay. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F refines the practical timing interpretation by stating that generalization benefits can occur at or even before norm-ratio trajectories intersect. v1 emphasized the intersection-based window of opportunity. The geometric explanation and existing applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents settings for the new ablations, including schedule matching, regularization strengths and switch-off points, and identifies JUWELS computing resources in its acknowledgments. Existing optimizer, initialization, learning-rate and LoRA configuration disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works and positioning relative to prior research are unchanged. A bibliography URL punctuation correction does not alter the cited work.

P1.justification: Section 3 gains a Preliminaries subsection, repeats relevant Appendix A definitions with short explanations, and reorganizes its roadmap. Contributions and regularization effects become bullet lists, and acknowledgments are added. Most narrative text remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds two ablation tables and relocates v1 Figure 14 from Appendix F into Section 4 as Figure 2. Other figures and tables are reflowed and renumbered, while existing plotted content is retained.

improvement.justification: The added schedule and timing checks in Tables 2–3 strengthen support for the existing switch-off recommendation. Main-text prerequisites, relocated illustrations and expanded proof details also improve accessibility. These gains are limited: the new ablations provide no additional uncertainty information, and the original results and applicability limitations remain.
